# Our first trip to Japan:


SmartHelio’s journey into a changing solar market


For more than a year, we had been working with our Japanese clients from a distance. This September, we finally had the chance to sit around the same table.


On SmartHelio’s first trip to Japan


, we met with **Photon Capital, NTT Anode Energy, ENEOS Renewables,** and **Voltaiyo** to hear directly from the teams using our products and discuss what comes next.


Between client workshops, **the Swiss-Japan Energy Days in Osaka, and Smart Energy Week Japan in Tokyo** , the trip gave us a much closer look at a solar market entering a new phase, and the people shaping where it goes next.


## Meeting our clients in person


The client workshops were at the centre of our visit. We shared the latest developments in GAIA, but more importantly, spent time understanding what our clients are seeing on the ground.


The conversations quickly became practical: **identifying performance losses that may not trigger an alarm, reducing time spent reviewing data and preparing reports, and adapting operations as BESS becomes a bigger part of the market.** We also heard how important it is for new technology to fit existing O&M workflows rather than add more work.


These discussions reflected a wider shift in Japan. As the market moves beyond the FIT-driven growth of the past, performance, operating costs, proactive O&M, and long-term asset value are becoming more important, alongside cybersecurity and data ownership.


For us, the takeaway was simple: Japan is not a copy-paste market. **GAIA needs to reflect how teams actually work in Japan, and what we learned during these workshops will directly shape what we build next.**


## Beyond the workshop room


Not every conversation happened in a meeting room. From lunch in Tokyo to sharing a traditional Japanese meal with clients, **some of the best conversations happened around the table** . After more than a year of working together through screens and across time zones, it was good to finally get to know the people behind the calls.


# Two events, two perspectives


Alongside our client workshops, we experienced two very different sides of Japan’s energy community.


Osaka


## Swiss-Japan Energy Days


**Our trip started in Osaka at the Swiss-Japan Energy Days** , where **we met people from across the energy ecosystem, from researchers and academics to utilities and large companies.** Govinda joined discussions on the future of energy and met the Swiss Ambassador to Japan, while Ohji gave his first-ever pitch, introducing SmartHelio to the audience. It was a memorable way to start our first trip to Japan.


Chiba


## Smart Energy Week


##


A week later, we were at Smart Energy Week in Chiba. We were invited to a private gathering where we had the chance to **meet executives from across Japan’s energy industry** , before spending three days at our booth speaking with people working across solar, BESS, O&M, and asset management. Those conversations gave us a much closer look at **the challenges companies are dealing with today and how they see the market evolving.**


**Osaka gave us a broader view of Japan’s energy ecosystem, while Chiba brought us closer to the industry itself.** Both gave us something we could never get from meetings at a distance: the chance to meet the people behind the market and learn directly from them.


# From monitoring assets to managing them


## Japan's solar market: from FIT to performance


## 1. Past: FIT-driven growth


After Fukushima, **strong FIT support** helped Japan rapidly expand solar capacity. The priority was building assets and securing predictable returns **plant performance optimisation** mattered less than it does today.


## 2.


Gaps that became visible


Advanced analytics are still developing, and O&M has often been **reactive fixing shutdowns** and major failures rather than catching **smaller performance losses, degradation, or early warning signs.** Asset-management processes are becoming more important too.


## 3. The market is now changing


As FIT support reduces, owners need to focus on **plant performance and energy yield** , operating cost, proactive and standardised O&M, **long-term asset value** , and better use of operational data.


## 4. Cybersecurity is becoming part of the discussion


Geopolitics is also playing an increasingly important role. **For energy** **infrastructure, cybersecurity, data ownership and control over where data is processed** are becoming extremely important. This means future analytics and AI solutions need to be not only intelligent, but also **secure, auditable and suitable for critical infrastructure.**


## What this means for SmartHelio


We see an opportunity to bring the experience and technology we have developed in Switzerland and Europe to Japan. But our workshops made one thing very clear: **Japan is not a copy-paste market.**


Some technologies and processes can be applied directly, while others need to be **adapted to Japanese O&M workflows, asset-management practices, security requirements** and the way decisions are made locally.


## Building the next phase in Japan


Our first trip to Japan gave us something that a year of online meetings could not: **the chance to sit down with our clients,** hear directly about the challenges they are facing, and experience the market for ourselves.


We came back to Switzerland with new ideas, stronger relationships, and plenty of feedback for the team. Some of what we learned will directly shape what we build next in GAIA, while other conversations opened doors we are excited to keep exploring.


Most importantly, this trip felt less like a first visit and more like **the beginning of our next chapter in Japan.** We are already looking forward to going back.
